inputs.goal: Discover the Kubernetes cluster resources, and deploy a MiniCluster starting at size 1 node with maximum cores available (tasks) for that node. Use the container ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax with ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy for flux.container.image and target run lmp -v x X -v y Y -v z Z -in in.reaxff.hns, where X Y and Z describe the problem size. You MUST deploy to the default namespace. It is up to you maximize the Figure of merit, k-atom or M-atom steps/s on one node. You MUST keep increasing X Y Z until the job does not complete or errors. If the run is successful, parse the log and get the FOM. If not, keep trying to deploy until it is fixed. Keep going until you deem optimized and then scale to 2 nodes. After you finish with 2 nodes, return all FOMs you have parsed, along with relevant reason and literature, the chosen X,Y, and Z in the format {"x": <value>, "y": <value>, "z", <value>, "foms": {"size-1": <value>. "size-2": <value>}, "reasons": "<logic>"}. You MUST pin the size after the first node and use the same problem size for subsequent experiments. You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1.

outputs.summary: The optimization process is complete. I found the optimal single-node problem size and then scaled the experiment to two nodes, achieving near-linear performance scaling.

final_fom.reasons: The optimization began by testing different problem sizes on a single node to maximize the Figure of Merit (FOM). A problem size of 10x10x10 yielded an FOM of 595.514 katom-step/s, while a larger size of 20x20x20 increased the FOM to 721.015 katom-step/s, indicating better resource utilization. A subsequent attempt with a 30x30x30 problem size failed due to an out-of-memory error, establishing the optimal single-node problem size at 20x20x20. This problem size was then used for a two-node experiment, which yielded an FOM of 1376 katom-step/s. This represents a scaling factor of approximately 1.9, which is considered excellent and demonstrates the efficiency of the framework for this application.
